simple.meaning: פּוֹטִיפַר (Pôwṭîyphar) is a Hebrew word meaning “Potiphar , an Egyptian.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פּוֹטִיפַר (H6318) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 37:36, with occurrences in Genesis.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פּוֹטִיפַר (H6318) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פּוֹטִיפַר (H6318) before moving outward to related references.

timeline.evidenceText: The Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.
Joseph was brought down to Egypt. Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites that had brought him down there.
